## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, so any mixed-case key written with `set` can never be read back with `get`. This breaks the main feature the pull request adds and must be fixed before merge.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set(key, value)` method and raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, with a matching comment update. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` stores the entry under `"Alpha"`, but `get` looks up `key.lower()` (app/cache.py:17), so `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` both return `None`. This breaks the rule in app/cache.py:14-15 that "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". — Callers who use mixed-case keys get silent cache misses, and those entries stay in `_store` because `get` never finds them to evict. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and add a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"` to `test_set_then_get_round_trip`, which currently sets only the lower-case `"alpha"` and so cannot catch this.
